Priya Singh: Heads-up — during the INT8/AWQ vs GPTQ bakeoff I noticed a consistent accuracy jump (worse) on llm-detox for the 24B model when using our AWQ INT8 profile. +2.7% false positives vs FP16.
Ethan Kim: Ooof. Is that global or concentrated in a few examples?
Priya Singh: Looks concentrated. Ran our per-layer activation scan, and layer 18, channel 1023 shows extreme skew in the post-activation distribution.
Maya Patel: Can you paste the scan output?
Priya Singh: Sure:
```
# ./tools/scan_outliers.py --model redwood/24b-v1 --quant awq-int8 --metric llm-detox --per-channel
layer 18: channel 1023: kurtosis=34.2, max=8.9, mean=0.05
layer 19: channel 512: kurtosis=3.1, max=1.2
... (truncated)
```
Jorge Alvarez: That kurtosis is wild. Sounds like an outlier channel blowing quant scale. Which quant backend did AWQ pick for that layer?
Priya Singh: AWQ used per-channel scaling but global-clamp fallback. Kernel selected: awq_int8_fast.
Ethan Kim: Two quick options: 1) clamp/clip that channel (per-channel clip), 2) force that layer to FP16 or GPTQ fallback, 3) rescale channel by median absolute deviation.
Maya Patel: We should avoid full FP16 for perf reasons. Maybe a hybrid: skip quant for that single channel or apply channel-level rescale + clip.
Jorge Alvarez: Agreed. Skipping a single channel in a weight matrix is cheap (mask it out to fp16 store) — need a quick prototype.
Priya Singh: I tried a quick hack: zeroed quant scale for channel 1023 and re-run eval -> delta drops to +0.4%. Throughput loss negligible in perf sim.
Ethan Kim: Nice. Can you share the command you used?
Priya Singh: ```
python quant_profiles/apply_channel_patch.py --model redwood/24b-v1 --layer 18 --channel 1023 --strategy zero_scale
# then run ./bench/eval_llm_detox.sh --model patched/24b-v1
```
Maya Patel: What's the risk of harming other benchmarks? We need to run a small eval matrix (toxicity, truthfulness, common-sense) before accepting.
Priya Singh: Already queued: tox, truth, gsm8k. CI bot will post results (Luca).
Luca (ci-bot): queued: run-1782501234: llm-detox, truthfulness, toxicity, gsm8k. Expected ~45m.
Jorge Alvarez: If zero_scale is risky, we could try per-channel affine rescale: multiply that channel by 0.3 and renormalize accompanying bias. Lower quant clip to 6 sigma.
Ethan Kim: Another idea: for AWQ, force per-channel symmetric quant for that layer (instead of asymmetric) — sometimes asymmetry amplifies small negative spikes.
Maya Patel: Good call. Also collect activation histograms pre/post patch and keep a diff to avoid silent regressions.
Priya Singh: I'll run: per-channel clip, symmetric quant, and single-channel skip. Will post the short log + perf numbers when done.
Ethan Kim: If the single-channel skip wins, we should add automation: detect kurtosis > X and auto-generate a patch suggestion during quant bakeoff.
Jorge Alvarez: Yeah — a small tool: detect channels with kurtosis>10 and max>6*std => suggest 'channel-rescue' patch. We can incorporate that into quant-profile auto-tuner.
Priya Singh: Filing a tiny RFC in docs: https://redwood.internal/quant/chan-rescue (draft).
Maya Patel: Thanks. If CI is green, let's apply the patch to the AWQ baseline and re-run the AWQ vs GPTQ comparison table.
Priya Singh: Will update thread with CI link and a short patch diff.
Ethan Kim: :thumbsup:
